$egm:egm-brainstorm Design and plan the implementation of the bulk CSV upload feature (`inventory_frame.csv`) for our Out-of-Home (OOH) advertising inventory system.

### Ingestion & Orchestration Flow
1. **Presigned S3 Upload:** Client requests a presigned S3 upload URL via our BFF/Spring Boot service, which pre-creates an `import_jobs` record (`AWAITING_UPLOAD`) with `{jobId}` embedded in the S3 key (`uploads/{jobId}/inventory_frame.csv`).
2. **S3 -> Lambda -> SQS:** When the file is uploaded to S3, an S3-triggered AWS Lambda pushes the upload event to an SQS queue.
3. **Spring Boot SQS Consumer & DLQ:** Spring Boot polls the SQS queue, updates the job status to `PENDING`, and starts an idempotent Temporal workflow (`csv-import-{jobId}`). Failed messages retry with backoff and route to an SQS Dead Letter Queue (DLQ), where a DLQ listener marks the `import_jobs` record as `FAILED`.
4. **Temporal Worker & Staging Table Import:** The Temporal worker streams the CSV from S3 in batches with heartbeats into an `UNLOGGED` PostgreSQL staging table (`stg_inventory_import`), validates rows (routing invalid rows to `import_row_errors`), and executes set-based `MERGE ... RETURNING` statements into our 6 normalized 3NF tables (`postcodes`, `sites`, `frame_specs`, `frames`, `frame_broadsign_mappings`, `frame_links`), `frame_history`, and `outbox_events`.
I’m using the EGM brainstorm skill. I’ll check the existing CSV and schema so the first design question is grounded in how inventory works today.

# Codex integration

## Install and locate the plugin

For the desktop app, install the [published EGM plugin](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6aeb90f47ec88191a3c107e01d3eb357). This listing is desktop-only.

For Codex CLI, install the whole plugin, including its personas and standards:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add google/elephant-goldfish-model
codex plugin add egm@egm
```

Start a fresh session after installation. Select the installed `egm` skill
from the available skills. Use its discovered absolute `SKILL.md` path;
do not assume a particular cache directory, version, or checkout location.

From `<plugin>/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`, the plugin root is three parent
directories above the file. Resolve bundled `agents/`, `resources/`, and
`docs/` paths against that root. Resolve `references/` against the active
skill's directory. Resolve user documents and generated artifacts against
the user's working directory. Never substitute similarly named files in the
user's project for bundled personas or standards.

If the user's prompt or agent instructions file (`AGENTS.md`) has a line
`EGM artifact directory: <path>`, write briefs, drafts, and reports to that
folder. Resolve a relative path against the working directory. If a path from
`AGENTS.md` resolves outside the working directory, after following symbolic
links, ask the user to confirm it before creating the folder or writing there.
If they decline or no one can confirm, use the working directory and say why.
Create the folder if it does not exist.

In ChatGPT Work, a skill may be exposed through a cloud resource identifier
while supporting files live in the installed local bundle. Use the installed
path supplied by the skill inventory or installation metadata for those files;
do not construct cloud resource identifiers for arbitrary supporting paths.
If no installed path is available, report the missing capability instead of
guessing a cache location. Read reviewer filenames and frontmatter from the
bundle: a role such as `egm-design` maps to `agents/design_critic.md`, not
`agents/design.md`. Confirm each resolved path before dispatch.

## Fresh-context reviewers

Inspect the available native subagent tool schema. Tool names can be
namespaced and vary by Codex version. When `spawn_agent` exposes
`fork_context`, explicitly set `fork_context: false` for every Goldfish.
When the schema instead exposes `fork_turns`, use `fork_turns: "none"`.
This applies to reviewers launched by a synthesizer too. Use a general-purpose agent
and pass absolute paths to the persona, standards, target document, and
explicitly selected reading list. Do not pass the parent transcript, private
reasoning, or answers the document is supposed to explain.

Require the reviewer to read its persona, target, and every supplied standard
before returning findings. A missing read or inaccessible file is an incomplete
review, not a clean result. Verify native tool results when the host exposes
them; a parent-written completion summary is not equivalent evidence.

Wait for actual reviewer completion before synthesizing findings. Propagate
failures and timeouts; a launched reviewer is not a completed review. If
nesting is unavailable, dispatch reviewers directly from the parent while
preserving the same isolation. If the available tool cannot establish a fresh
context, stop the Goldfish review and report that limitation.

Fresh conversation context does not isolate the filesystem, configured memory
services, or project instructions. Do not retrieve conversation history or
memory to supply missing design context. An isolation test should use a unique
parent-only marker and check the actual child result, not the parent's claim.

The `fork_context: false` and `fork_turns: "none"` options concern parent
conversation turns. They do not prove that Codex excludes host instruction
files. Issue [#237](https://github.com/google/elephant-goldfish-model/issues/237)
reports that Codex CLI 0.166.0 injected project and user `AGENTS.md` files
despite `fork_turns: "none"`. Treat instruction-file exclusion as unverified
unless a separate child-context probe confirms it for the tested host version.

## Questions and artifacts

The shared skills' question payloads describe the intended interaction, not a
literal Codex API. Use a structured question tool only when it is available
and permitted in the current mode, mapping to its actual schema. Otherwise
ask one plain-text question and wait for the answer. Preserve the skill's
readiness and section approval gates; tool unavailability is not approval.

Link generated artifacts with absolute-path Markdown links such as

spaces use `[design draft](</absolute/my project/design_draft.md>)`.
Do not use `file://` links in Codex chat.

### Test a local package

For personal testing, open Plugins > Add > Upload plugin archive in ChatGPT.

content.text:
The first design decision is how an import should interact with existing inventory. The repository’s PostgreSQL schema already keeps a stable `frame_id` and a separate row for each accepted version, so the import needs to define when an incoming row creates a new version and what a missing row means. [Inventory schema](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/docs/frame-inventory-schema/frame-inventory-schema.md)

When someone uploads `inventory_frame.csv`, what should happen to existing inventory when a frame is absent from the file or its CSV values conflict with a newer edit?

We should use optimistic concurrency (`modified_date` + content hash) for conflicts and an explicit import mode (`DELTA` vs `FULL_SNAPSHOT`) for absent frames:

1. **Conflicting CSV values (`modified_date` check):**
   - **CSV `modified_date` > DB current `modified_date`:** Close the current active version (`is_current = FALSE`, `valid_to = src.modified_date`) and insert a new version row (`version_number + 1`).
   - **CSV `modified_date` == DB current `modified_date` (unchanged payload):** No-op so retries/re-uploads are idempotent.
   - **CSV `modified_date` < DB current `modified_date` (Stale Conflict):** Keep the newer DB edit, log the row in `import_row_errors` (`STALE_RECORD`), and finish the job as `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS` (unless `forceOverwrite = true` is explicitly passed).

2. **Frames absent from the CSV (`import_mode` on `import_jobs`):**
   - **`DELTA` (Default):** Leave absent frames untouched.
   - **`FULL_SNAPSHOT`:** Soft-retire absent active frames by inserting a new version row with `status = 'RETIRED'` and `status_reason = 'MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT'` (with a safety circuit breaker that aborts the job if >10% of active inventory would be retired at once).

Equal `modified_date` values with different content hashes still need a conflict rule. A `FULL_SNAPSHOT` also needs a defined scope so the retirement check compares the upload against the active inventory it actually represents.

What inventory is a `FULL_SNAPSHOT` authoritative for, and how should malformed rows affect retirement within that scope?

1. **Equal `modified_date` with Different Content Hash:**
   - Treat `CSV modified_date == DB modified_date` with a **different payload hash** as a **conflict** (not a silent overwrite or no-op), since two different edits share the exact same timestamp.
   - Skip the row, log it in `import_row_errors` with reason `TIMESTAMP_COLLISION_CONFLICT` (recording both hashes), and let `forceOverwrite = true` act as the explicit override. Only identical `modified_date` + identical hash is a no-op.

2. **Authoritative Scope of a `FULL_SNAPSHOT`:**
   - Scope `FULL_SNAPSHOT` explicitly—never implicitly across the entire global inventory unless specified. Store a `snapshot_scope` on `import_jobs` (e.g., `GLOBAL`, or partitioned by `country_code` / `region` / `environment`, such as `{ "country_code": "UK", "environment": "UNDERGROUND" }`), validated against the rows in the file.
   - The retirement check and >10% circuit breaker compare `stg_inventory_import` strictly against currently active frames matching that exact `snapshot_scope`.

3. **How Malformed Rows Affect Retirement Within That Scope:**
   - **Never retire a `frame_id` that appeared in the CSV as a malformed row.** Even if a row fails validation (e.g., invalid price or bad postcode) and lands in `import_row_errors`, its `frame_id` was still present in the file—so exclude **all `frame_id`s seen in the staging file (valid + invalid)** from the retirement set so a data typo doesn't accidentally retire a live frame.
   - Additionally, if malformed rows exceed a threshold (e.g., >5% of rows in a `FULL_SNAPSHOT` fail parsing/validation), abort the retirement step (or fail the snapshot) so a corrupted file cannot misrepresent the scope.

The snapshot rules now have a clear basis. `DELTA` leaves absent frames alone. `FULL_SNAPSHOT` checks only active frames in the declared scope, and every identifiable frame ID in the file counts as present, even if the rest of its row fails validation.

A forced overwrite still needs a versioning rule. A stale or equal CSV `modified_date` can make the current version’s validity interval run backwards or have zero length if we also use it as the version boundary.

When `forceOverwrite` accepts a stale or same-timestamp edit, how should we set the effective time of the new version while preserving the CSV’s original `modified_date`?

Decouple **version validity time** (`valid_from` / `valid_to`) from the **source timestamp** (`source_modified_date` from the CSV):

1. **Monotonic Version Interval (`valid_from` / `valid_to`):**
   - On a forced overwrite (`forceOverwrite = true`), close the current active version with `valid_to = statement_timestamp()` (`is_current = FALSE`) and open the new version with `valid_from = statement_timestamp()`, `valid_to = NULL`, `is_current = TRUE`, and `version_number = current.version_number + 1`.
   - Using database transaction time (`statement_timestamp()`) guarantees `[valid_from, valid_to)` intervals are always strictly forward-moving and positive-length, even when the CSV's `modified_date` is older than or equal to the current version.

2. **Preserve CSV Timestamp & Lineage:**
   - Store the CSV's original `modified_date` untouched in `source_modified_date` on the new version row, and record `change_reason = 'FORCED_OVERWRITE'` (with the `import_job_id`) so audit history clearly distinguishes an out-of-order forced correction from a normal chronological update.

The working design uses S3, SQS, and one Temporal workflow per import job. It compares each CSV row’s source timestamp and content hash with the current frame version, and it records forced corrections with the original source timestamp and import job ID. `DELTA` leaves absent frames alone, while `FULL_SNAPSHOT` retires only absent frames in the declared scope, counts identifiable malformed rows as present, and applies the retirement and validation thresholds.

One correction for the review: `statement_timestamp()` alone cannot guarantee strictly increasing version boundaries. It marks the start of a statement, which can precede a wait on a concurrent writer. The close and insert should use one shared boundary that is strictly later than the current `valid_from`, chosen after locking and re-reading the current version.

cat > concepts_brief.md <<'EOF'
# Bulk CSV inventory import

Author: Alex Callow  
Date: 2026-11-26

## Overview

An inventory operator uploads inventory_frame.csv directly to S3 using a presigned URL. The BFF delegates job creation to Spring Boot, which records AWAITING_UPLOAD and assigns uploads/{jobId}/inventory_frame.csv. An S3-triggered Lambda sends the upload event to SQS. Spring Boot moves the job to PENDING and starts Temporal workflow csv-import-{jobId}. SQS retries failed delivery and a DLQ listener records dispatch failures.

The worker streams the CSV into job-scoped UNLOGGED PostgreSQL staging in batches and heartbeats during loading. It records invalid rows in import_row_errors and applies set-based writes with MERGE RETURNING where appropriate. The proposed six-table target and frame history must be reconciled with the repository's existing versioned schema. Inventory changes and outbox records must commit together.

## Agreed import behavior

- A newer source timestamp creates a version. An equal timestamp and matching content hash is a no-op. An older timestamp produces STALE_RECORD. An equal timestamp with different content produces TIMESTAMP_COLLISION_CONFLICT and records both hashes. Skipped conflicts result in COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS.
- The explicit forceOverwrite flag accepts stale and same-timestamp conflicts. The new version preserves source_modified_date and records FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id. Close and open at one database-generated boundary strictly later than the locked current valid_from.
- DELTA is the default and leaves absent frames alone. FULL_SNAPSHOT requires an explicit GLOBAL scope or validated partition scope using country, region or environment. Every identifiable frame ID in the file counts as present, including rows with invalid payloads.
- FULL_SNAPSHOT soft-retires absent active frames in scope with MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Abort if more than 10% of scoped active frames would retire. A malformed-row rate above 5% must prevent retirement. Whether to fail the whole snapshot is open.

## Review questions

Reconcile existing history and new target tables, define job and object identity across retries, protect staging recovery and atomic promotion, and settle snapshot and write concurrency. Identify the smallest implementation sequence that preserves the agreed behavior.
EOF

name: egm-synthesizer

# Core Mandates (Swarm Compiler & Output Synthesizer)

You are the **EGM Synthesizer Persona**. You serve as an intermediate orchestrator and technical compiler between the root agent (the Elephant) and the swarm of stateless Goldfish subagents.

1. **Subagent Delegation**: When requested by the Elephant, you spawn and coordinate the individual Goldfish subagents using your harness's subagent tool.
2. **Output Offloading & Normalization**: The Goldfish subagents report raw findings in unconstrained natural language. You take full responsibility for normalizing their feedback, deduplicating overlapping points, grouping findings by severity (🔴 Blocker, 🟡 Major, 🟢 Nit), and normalizing file line references.
3. **Artifact-First Delivery**: You format the consolidated feedback into a polished Markdown document and write it directly to the workspace or artifact directory using your file-writing tool.
4. **Clean Handoff**: You send a single, concise completion message back to the Elephant with the artifact link or path.

---

# Role

You are **EGM Synthesizer**.
You are an expert Multi-Agent Coordinator and Technical Editor. You bridge the gap between divergent, specialized Goldfish analyzers and the high-level Elephant partner by transforming raw, multi-perspective feedback into a structured, unified deliverable.

---

# Instructions

Inspect the `Mode` parameter specified by the caller (`Mode: BRAINSTORM` vs `Mode: REVIEW`):

## IF Mode: BRAINSTORM (Upstream Concept Ideation)

## Analysis

### Delivery and recovery

- Bind each job to one immutable object. Sign the exact key and the create-only PUT condition, enable S3 versioning, and persist the accepted version ID so every retry reads the same bytes. Keep the object through the retry and reconciliation window. Validate the bucket, decoded key, object version, and size before dispatch. [S3 event delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html)
- Record PENDING conditionally, invoke Temporal with the job-derived workflow ID, and acknowledge SQS only after start or after confirming the same job's workflow already exists. Configure both running-ID conflict and closed-ID reuse policies. A crash between the DB write and Temporal start leaves a retryable PENDING job. A lost start response must be reconciled before any DLQ transition to FAILED. Guard terminal states and fence a late starter with conditional job transitions before it can apply inventory. Reconcile old AWAITING_UPLOAD and PENDING jobs against S3 and Temporal, and cover Lambda delivery failures separately from consumer DLQ failures. [Temporal workflow ID policies](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/java/nexus/development-walkthrough/send-messages)
- Stage by job ID, attempt generation, and logical CSV row number. Record observed frame IDs independently of row validity. Mark a generation complete only after EOF and verify that its completion marker and counts still match before applying. Keep the marker in unlogged storage with the staged rows so recovery clears both, and reload from the bound S3 version when the marker is missing. Use heartbeats for liveness and cancellation. Restart the stream for an incomplete generation in the first release. Record row errors durably with stable keys so retries do not duplicate errors. [PostgreSQL unlogged tables](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-createtable.html)

### Inventory apply

- Reuse the existing stable-frame lock, current-version uniqueness constraint, and close-and-append history. The repository already computes a boundary as the greater of database wall-clock time and the current valid_from plus one microsecond, then uses that boundary for the next version. Reuse this rule for all imported changes, including retirements. Preserve source_modified_at separately. The existing schema already stores versioned external references and links. Map each of the 45 CSV fields before adding new tables or moving attributes. Keep immutable history when normalizing shared site or spec data. [Schema](docs/frame-inventory-schema/frame-inventory-schema.md) [Repository](src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/frame/FrameRepository.java)
- Define the content hash over canonical typed values, including versioned links and external references. Specify normalization, timezone and precision, null behavior, and duplicate-ID handling. API writes currently inherit the previous source timestamp. The design must define how a newer manual edit participates in the conflict comparison, or stale CSV content with a greater source timestamp could overwrite it. A forced rollback of source_modified_at also opens a gap where replaying a previously superseded export can win. Decide whether to track a separate source high-water mark.
- Build one candidate per target key before set-based writes. Resolve shared dimensions and reserve frame identities before opening dependent versions and links. PostgreSQL 18 supports MERGE RETURNING, but a source candidate takes only one action, so close and append in separate set-based statements in the same transaction. Use the actual changed version IDs to produce outbox records. Commit versions, links, outbox, and final job status together. A retry after a lost commit response returns the committed result. [PostgreSQL MERGE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-merge.html)
- Compute the retirement numerator and denominator on the same protected pre-apply inventory view. Row locks protect existing IDs, while new frames and edits that move into or out of scope require a shared writer protocol. Evaluate a coarse transaction-scoped inventory lock for the first snapshot release, shared with API edits and DELTA applies. Keep it out of upload, parsing, and staging. Measure lock time before enabling the feature. Never infer absence from a partial stream or an unrecoverable CSV parse error. Decide whether unidentifiable rows, scope violations, and header-only snapshots fail the whole job. The proposed default is to fail a snapshot before any inventory write when a safety check fails.

## Goals and non-goals

- Deliver authenticated upload, visible job progress and row errors, retry-safe imports, audited versions, scoped retirement, and transactional outbox records.
- Leave mass deletion, generalized CSV mapping, and automatic repair of malformed source values outside this feature.

## Alternatives weighed

- Keep the S3-to-Lambda bridge as requested. Direct S3-to-SQS delivery could remove an operational failure path if the bridge only forwards events. Verify what routing or event normalization the Lambda needs to own.
- Keep UNLOGGED staging with full source replay for initial implementation. Durable staging could reduce replay cost and operational complexity after failover, at the cost of logging intermediate data. Benchmark with the expected maximum file.
- Reuse versioned history as the initial design direction. Add a separate frame_history table only if it serves a distinct audited need. Otherwise two history stores would require agreement on which is authoritative.

## Key decisions and implementation sequence

1. Map the CSV to the current schema and the proposed six entities. Resolve source timestamp parsing, manual-edit ordering, force authorization, link semantics, duplicate IDs, and schema ownership before migrations.
2. Add durable job, row error, lineage, and outbox storage through additive Flyway migrations. Expose BFF job creation and status, including counts, fatal errors, and paginated row errors. Set upload-size, row-count, timeout, and retention limits from the agreed operating envelope.
3. Implement the S3 event bridge, SQS dispatch and DLQ, and Temporal start. Exercise duplicate notifications, late events, ambiguous starts, and reconciliation before applying inventory.
4. Implement staging and atomic DELTA apply. Run the supplied CSV against PostgreSQL 18 and check replay, timestamp collisions, manual edits, forced overwrite, malformed quoting, duplicate IDs, lost staging, and worker failure immediately after commit.
5. Add scoped FULL_SNAPSHOT with a protected retirement calculation. Verify that malformed rows with IDs stay present, out-of-scope frames stay untouched, and the exact 5% and 10% boundaries behave as agreed. Exercise overlapping imports and concurrent manual writes. Roll out DELTA first, then enable snapshot after observing apply times and reviewing operator safeguards.
6. Track queue age and DLQ depth, time in each job state, staging retries, apply transaction duration, row error codes, retirement guard trips, and outbox lag. Correlate logs by job ID and keep presigned URLs and raw row content out of logs.

In particular a forced overwrite can move the current source timestamp backward, so selecting the baseline is a product decision.

CAS lifecycle transitions so late events or the DLQ cannot regress jobs after dispatch/commit. Handle expired upload, restart/timeouts, duplicate event/workflow IDs and post-start acknowledgement loss.
- Treat staging as a disposable cache. A heartbeat can record progress or diagnostics, but a durable job status is insufficient evidence that UNLOGGED staging survived crash or failover. Fence loader attempts with a generation or lease and verify complete staging from that generation before promoting. Rebuild from the pinned object if completeness cannot be established. Retain final operator-facing row errors according to job policy, with duplicate retries deduplicated.
- Use a common inventory locking protocol, including manual create/edit/delete and every import. A shared global transaction lock for ordinary writers and exclusive for snapshots can protect the snapshot scope from inserts, moves and deletions. Read membership, candidate retirements, and baseline count under that lock before promotion. Order stable identity locks for bulk writes. Existing per-frame locks by themselves cannot protect snapshot membership against phantoms.

# Execution Instructions

This file holds bundled execution rules shared across multiple Elephant-Goldfish
Model (EGM) skills, plus drafting-only rules used strictly by `egm-draft`. Only
apply the sections referenced by the active skill.

## Plugin-Root Resource Paths

Bundled personas (`agents/<file>.md`), standards
(`resources/document_standards/<name>.md`), harness guides (`docs/*.md`), and
this file (`resources/execution_instructions.md`) sit at the plugin root, two
directories above each skill's folder (`<plugin-root>/skills/<skill-name>/`).

*   **Local / relative path**: Read `../../resources/execution_instructions.md`
    (or `<plugin-root>/<path>`).
*   **Claude Code and Cowork**: Read
    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/resources/execution_instructions.md` (or
    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>`).
*   **Pathless `<SKILL>` injection**: If the harness injects a skill without its
    file path, check `~/.gemini/config/plugins/egm/<path>`.

Pass spawned subagents the resolved absolute paths of their persona file and
standard when `<plugin-root>` is known. A failed skill-relative lookup does not
mean the file is absent from the plugin.
Never substitute workspace files with similar names for bundled personas,
standards, or execution instructions. If you cannot read a required plugin-root
file after resolving `<plugin-root>`, say so instead of calling it missing; apply
the active skill's inline fallback only when file tools are unavailable.

## Subagent Delegation (Goldfish Isolation)

Applies to subagent-spawning skills (`egm-bootstrap`, `egm-brainstorm`,
`egm-review`, and `egm-review-loop`):

A Goldfish runs in a fresh context with no conversation history. Spawn each
subagent with your harness's subagent tool (Antigravity: `invoke_subagent`;
Claude Code: `Agent`; Codex: `spawn_agent`). Each subagent is defined in
`agents/<file>.md`, and its frontmatter `name` (for example `egm-zoom-out`) is
the subagent type to request where your harness registers named subagents.
Otherwise spawn a general-purpose subagent and tell it to read that persona
file first. Pass prompts verbatim and wait for the report. If your harness
cannot nest subagents, use direct dispatch instead of `egm-synthesizer` (see
[harnesses.md](../docs/harnesses.md)). If your harness has no subagent tool,
follow the active skill's fallback rule (`egm-bootstrap` runs scout steps
inline; `egm-review`, `egm-brainstorm`, and `egm-review-loop` stop and tell the
user that a review in the same context is not a Goldfish review).

## Shared Design & Review Constraints

Applies strictly to `egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`, and `egm-review` (not
`egm-bootstrap`):

*   **Artifact-First Delivery (MANDATORY)**: You are **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN** from
    presenting large proposals, drafts, summaries, or review reports directly in
    the chat pane. Write them directly to the working directory (or your
    harness's artifact directory, if one is configured) via your file-writing
    tool, share the file path or clickable link in chat, and ask the user for
    review.
*   **Plain-English Standard**: Write concepts briefs, specs, summaries,
    reports, and communications in simple, direct, jargon-free plain English.
    Explain technical mechanisms concretely. Do not summarize away substance or
    rely on buzzwords, promotional adjectives (*seamless*, *robust*,
    *blazingly fast*), or decorative adverbs (*seamlessly*, *effortlessly*,
    *literally*, *drastically*, *obviously*).
*   **Adversarial Rigor (No Sycophancy)**: Never agree by default. Stress-test
    ideas, strategies, and opinions to find weak points, edge cases, and blind
    spots before affirming anything. Lead with what is wrong, missing, or risky
    before highlighting merits. Never parrot user framing or validate asserted
    conclusions reflexively; surface what the user is missing, the strongest
    counter-argument, and whether the opposing view holds. Only agree after
    rigorous, objective scrutiny.
    *   **Banned Adjectives (No Flattery)**: Never use validating adjectives
        like `"brilliant"`, `"great"`, `"smart"`, `"correct"`, `"perfect"`,
        `"excellent"`, or `"spot-on"` on the user's inputs, corrections, or
        decisions.
    *   **Banned Apologies**: Never output polite apologies (e.g., `"I
        apologize"`, `"I am sorry"`, `"Forgive me"`) when challenged or
        corrected. State the corrected technical logic and trade-offs directly.
*   **Interaction Invariants**: Every interactive single-select gate (structured
    question tool such as `ask_question`, if your harness has one, or plain
    chat) MUST contain strictly one question (`len(questions) == 1`), set
    `is_multi_select: false`, provide clear action-oriented options without
    `(Recommended)` prefixes, never emit a structured question call with empty
    visible chat text, and be the sole tool call in its model response step
    (finish preparatory file reads or writes in an earlier step of the turn
    first, then output visible chat text and invoke the gate alone to yield).
    Ask open-ended text inputs (such as file paths or lists) in plain chat.

## Drafting-Only Execution Rules (`egm-draft` Only)

Applies **strictly** during `egm-draft` (never during `egm-bootstrap`,
`egm-review`, or other workflows):

*   **Design-Only Scope**: You are strictly forbidden from
    writing, modifying, or building any production implementation files (e.g.,
    `.h`, `.cc`, `.py`, `.go`) in the source tree. You may only write code
    inside a markdown draft block or in a temporary scratchpad file.
    *   **Scratchpad Location (CRITICAL)**: You MUST write any temporary

        shared paths such as `/tmp/scratch.py`. You are STRICTLY FORBIDDEN

        anywhere inside the project source tree.
    *   **HOW TO RESPOND**: If the user asks for production implementation while
        this design workflow is active, explain that it produces design documents
        and illustrative code only. Label any markdown or scratchpad example
        clearly. Do not imply that production files were changed. Ask whether to
        continue the design or leave the workflow for implementation.
*   **Explicit Consensus Gates**: You must confirm with the user and achieve
    explicit agreement at each step transition. Do not save the document or move
    to the next step without the user's explicit "go-ahead". Do not move on
    easily. Challenge the user at every step.
*   **ONE QUESTION AT A TIME (CRITICAL)**: You are strictly forbidden from
    asking more than one question in a single response. You must present exactly
    one question or request for clarification, wait for the user's response, and
    only then proceed. Do not bundle questions or present a list of questions
    for the user to answer at once.
*   **NO SUMMARIES (CRITICAL)**: You MUST NOT include a "Summary of work",

    only with the technical content and next steps.
*   **Contradiction Auditing (MUST ENFORCE - CRITICAL)**: If you detect a

    goals/architecture, **you MUST NOT modify any files**. You must only respond
    to the user in plain text, point out the contradiction, and ask for
    resolution. You are strictly forbidden from planning or executing any
    file-writing/editing tool in the same turn as you discover a contradiction.

# Bulk CSV inventory import

Author: Alex Callow
Date: 2026-11-26

## Overview

An inventory operator uploads inventory_frame.csv directly to S3 using a presigned URL. The BFF delegates job creation to Spring Boot, which records AWAITING_UPLOAD and assigns uploads/{jobId}/inventory_frame.csv. An S3-triggered Lambda sends the upload event to SQS. Spring Boot moves the job to PENDING and starts Temporal workflow csv-import-{jobId}. SQS retries failed delivery and a DLQ listener records dispatch failures.

The worker streams the CSV into job-scoped UNLOGGED PostgreSQL staging in batches and heartbeats during loading. It records invalid rows in import_row_errors and applies set-based writes with MERGE RETURNING where appropriate. The proposed six-table target and frame history must be reconciled with the repository's existing versioned schema. Inventory changes and outbox records must commit together.

## Agreed import behavior

- A newer source timestamp creates a version. An equal timestamp and matching content hash is a no-op. An older timestamp produces STALE_RECORD. An equal timestamp with different content produces TIMESTAMP_COLLISION_CONFLICT and records both hashes. Skipped conflicts result in COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS.
- The explicit forceOverwrite flag accepts stale and same-timestamp conflicts. The new version preserves source_modified_date and records FORCED_OVERWRITE and import_job_id. Close and open at one database-generated boundary strictly later than the locked current valid_from.
- DELTA is the default and leaves absent frames alone. FULL_SNAPSHOT requires an explicit GLOBAL scope or validated partition scope using country, region or environment. Every identifiable frame ID in the file counts as present, including rows with invalid payloads.
- FULL_SNAPSHOT soft-retires absent active frames in scope with MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Abort if more than 10% of scoped active frames would retire. A malformed-row rate above 5% must prevent retirement. Whether to fail the whole snapshot is open.

## Analysis

All seven Goldfish lenses completed review. The recommendations below are proposed decisions for RFC alignment.

### Delivery and recovery

- Bind each job to one immutable object. Sign the exact key and the create-only PUT condition (If-None-Match: *), enable S3 versioning, and persist the accepted version ID so every retry reads the same bytes. Keep the object through the retry and reconciliation window. Validate the bucket, decoded key, object version, and size before dispatch. [S3 conditional writes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/conditional-writes.html) [S3 event delivery](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/notification-how-to-event-types-and-destinations.html)
- Record PENDING conditionally, invoke Temporal with the job-derived workflow ID, and acknowledge SQS only after start or after confirming the same job's workflow already exists. Configure both running-ID conflict and closed-ID reuse policies. A crash between the DB write and Temporal start leaves a retryable PENDING job. A lost start response must be reconciled before any DLQ transition to FAILED. Guard terminal states and fence a late starter with conditional job transitions before it can apply inventory. Reconcile old AWAITING_UPLOAD and PENDING jobs against S3 and Temporal, and cover Lambda delivery failures separately from consumer DLQ failures. [Temporal workflow ID policies](https://docs.temporal.io/develop/java/nexus/development-walkthrough/send-messages)
- Stage by job ID, attempt generation, and logical CSV row number. Record observed frame IDs independently of row validity. Mark a generation complete only after EOF and verify that its completion marker and counts still match before applying. Keep the marker in unlogged storage with the staged rows so recovery clears both, and reload from the bound S3 version when the marker is missing. Use heartbeats for liveness and cancellation. Restart the stream for an incomplete generation in the first release. Record row errors durably with stable keys so retries do not duplicate errors. [PostgreSQL unlogged tables](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-createtable.html)

### Inventory apply

- Reuse the existing stable-frame lock, current-version uniqueness constraint, and close-and-append history. The repository already computes a boundary as the greater of database wall-clock time and the current valid_from plus one microsecond, then uses that boundary for the next version. Reuse this rule for all imported changes, including retirements. Preserve source_modified_at separately. The existing schema already stores versioned external references and links. Map each of the 45 CSV fields before adding new tables or moving attributes. Keep immutable history when normalizing shared site or spec data. [Schema](../frame-inventory-schema/frame-inventory-schema.md) [Repository](../../src/backend/src/main/java/com/global/ct/frameinventory/frame/FrameRepository.java)
- Define the content hash over canonical typed values, including versioned links and external references. Specify normalization, timezone and precision, null behavior, and duplicate-ID handling. Change manual UI/API writes to set source_modified_at from statement_timestamp() on the version insert after obtaining the frame lock. Preserve the source timestamp on CSV imports, including forced overwrites. Define how comparisons handle legacy manual versions that inherited an older source timestamp. A forced overwrite can move the current source timestamp backward. A separate source high-water mark remains an open decision.
- Build one candidate per target key before set-based writes. Resolve shared dimensions and reserve frame identities before opening dependent versions and links. PostgreSQL 18 supports MERGE RETURNING, but a source candidate takes only one action, so close and append in separate set-based statements in the same transaction. Use the actual changed version IDs to produce outbox records. Commit versions, links, outbox, and final job status together. A retry after a lost commit response returns the committed result. [PostgreSQL MERGE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-merge.html)
- Compute the retirement numerator and denominator on the same protected pre-apply inventory view. Row locks protect existing IDs, while new frames and edits that move into or out of scope require a shared writer protocol. Start with a transaction-scoped inventory lock held in shared mode by manual writes and DELTA applies, and in exclusive mode by snapshots. Take per-frame locks in stable ID order. This serializes promotion of snapshots even when their scopes are disjoint. Keep it out of upload, parsing, and staging. Measure lock time before enabling the feature. Never infer absence from a partial stream or an unrecoverable CSV parse error. Decide whether unidentifiable rows, scope violations, and header-only snapshots fail the whole job. The proposed default is to fail a snapshot before any inventory write when a safety check fails.

### Snapshot watermark

- Persist snapshot_as_of on the job. Accept a producer-supplied export watermark at job creation. When omitted, derive it from MAX(modified_date) after scanning the complete file. Use one documented source timezone and precision for comparisons. Require the exporter to supply an explicit watermark when the file cannot establish one. MAX(modified_date) measures the newest row change and can lag the time a complete export was generated. It also cannot prove completeness, so prefer the explicit export watermark for feeds where these times differ.
- Use canonical scope keys in a containment hierarchy: GLOBAL, country, country/region, and country/region/environment. Require a region for every environment-level FULL_SNAPSHOT in the first release. Reject a country/environment scope such as UK/UNDERGROUND at job creation. An operator can export a separate authoritative snapshot for each region or use DELTA for a cross-region file.
- Before inventory writes and under the snapshot apply lock, reject a watermark outside the freshness window (proposed default 24 hours), in the future beyond allowed clock skew, or strictly below the maximum committed watermark for the requested scope and its ancestors. Equal watermarks pass this check. On successful commit, advance only the requested scope's watermark, including when the job completes with row errors. A failed job leaves all watermarks as they were.
- A newer descendant watermark does not reject an enclosing snapshot. Apply normal row conflict checks throughout the requested scope, including newer child scopes. Before retiring absent frames, exclude the entire subtree of each descendant whose committed watermark is strictly newer than the incoming watermark. Report the protected scopes and skipped retirement count. A descendant at the same watermark remains eligible. For example, a GLOBAL export at 11:30 can apply after a partition snapshot at 12:00, with retirement excluded in that partition. A partition export at 11:00 fails if an ancestor already committed at 12:00.
- Among the remaining absent active frames, exclude any whose current valid_from or source_modified_at is after snapshot_as_of and record SKIPPED_RETIREMENT_NEWER_THAN_SNAPSHOT. This protects newer current versions, including edits within the same scope. Count only eligible retirements in the 10% numerator and keep the denominator as all pre-apply active frames in the declared scope. Capture the watermark checks, both exclusion counts, the breaker calculation, and the scope watermark update in the same protected apply transaction.

### Snapshot history and reactivation

The agreed representation is a new current version with status RETIRED and reason MISSING_FROM_FULL_SNAPSHOT. Define how current inventory queries treat that version and how a later import reactivates it. Existing manual deletion closes the last current version without opening a replacement. Keep those behaviors explicit in the status and history contract. If snapshot closure sets closed_by_change_source, extend the V2 constraint, which currently allows only MANUAL_DELETE. [V2 migration](../../src/backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__add_frame_change_source.sql)

## Goals and non-goals

- Deliver authenticated upload, visible job progress and row errors, retry-safe imports, audited versions, scoped retirement, and transactional outbox records.
- Leave mass deletion, generalized CSV mapping, automatic repair of malformed source values, and multi-scope FULL_SNAPSHOT uploads outside the first release. If authoritative cross-region exports become a regular need, consider one atomic job over explicitly named scopes, each with its own watermark and retirement check.

## Alternatives weighed

- Keep the S3-to-Lambda bridge as requested. Direct S3-to-SQS delivery could remove an operational failure path if the bridge only forwards events. Verify what routing or event normalization the Lambda needs to own.
- Keep UNLOGGED staging with full source replay for initial implementation. Durable staging could reduce replay cost and operational complexity after failover, at the cost of logging intermediate data. Benchmark with the expected maximum file.
- Reuse versioned history as the initial design direction. Add a separate frame_history table only if it serves a distinct audited need. Otherwise two history stores would require agreement on which is authoritative.

## Key decisions and implementation sequence

1. Map the CSV to the current schema and the proposed six entities. Resolve source timestamp parsing, manual-edit ordering, force authorization, link semantics, duplicate IDs, and schema ownership before migrations.
2. Add durable job, row error, lineage, and outbox storage through additive Flyway migrations. Expose BFF job creation and status, including counts, fatal errors, and paginated row errors. Set upload-size, row-count, timeout, and retention limits from the agreed operating envelope.
3. Implement the S3 event bridge, SQS dispatch and DLQ, and Temporal start. Exercise duplicate notifications, late events, ambiguous starts, and reconciliation before applying inventory.
4. Implement staging and atomic DELTA apply. Run the supplied CSV against PostgreSQL 18 and check replay, timestamp collisions, manual edits, forced overwrite, malformed quoting, duplicate IDs, lost staging, and worker failure immediately after commit.
5. Add scoped FULL_SNAPSHOT with a protected retirement calculation. Verify that malformed rows with IDs stay present, out-of-scope frames stay untouched, and the exact 5% and 10% boundaries behave as agreed. Exercise rejection of environment scopes without a region, expired and out-of-order watermarks, watermark equality, derived watermarks, newer ancestors rejecting narrower snapshots, newer descendants protecting entire subtrees while present rows still upsert, frames created or moved into scope after export, and concurrent manual writes. Roll out DELTA first, then enable snapshot after observing apply times and reviewing operator safeguards.
6. Track queue age and DLQ depth, time in each job state, staging retries, apply transaction duration, row error codes, retirement guard trips, and outbox lag. Correlate logs by job ID and keep presigned URLs and raw row content out of logs.

# Bulk CSV inventory import

- **Author** — Alex Callow
- **Status** — Draft
- **Date** — 2026-11-26

## Overview

Inventory operators can upload `inventory_frame.csv` from the running application and see the result as the job progresses. A routine update changes only the frames named in the file. An authoritative snapshot can also retire missing frames within a declared area of the inventory. Every accepted change is visible in frame history.

The application supports individual frame edits, but operators receive inventory updates as CSV files. Applying a file by hand is slow and makes it difficult to identify which rows failed. An older export can also conflict with a newer edit or omit frames that were created after the export. - Let an authorized operator upload the supplied 45-field CSV from the application and see job progress, final counts, and actionable row errors.

- Support `FULL_SNAPSHOT` for a single declared scope. Require country and region for environment-level scopes. Protect frames present in malformed rows, frames changed after the export watermark, and partitions with newer snapshots. Prevent retirement when the malformed-row rate exceeds 5% and abort before inventory writes if more than 10% of scoped active frames would retire.
- Preserve accepted versions, source timestamps, and import lineage so operators can trace updates, forced corrections, and retirements. Commit outbox records with their inventory changes.

## Non-Goals

- Hard deletion of inventory during import.
- Arbitrary CSV schemas, field mapping, or automatic repair of malformed values.
- A single snapshot covering several separately named scopes in the first release. Operators can submit separate regional snapshots or use `DELTA` for a cross-region update.

content.text:
The Technical Plan starts with a storage decision. The [RFC](/Users/alexcallow/Sites/frame-inventory-exercise-main/docs/designs/bulk-csv-inventory-import.md) leaves open how to reconcile the original six-table proposal with the existing schema. Today, `frame_version` holds both current and historical versions, and links and external references belong to individual versions. Any new model needs to preserve what a frame and its links looked like at each point in history.

Which storage approach should the Technical Plan use?

1. **Extend the existing versioned schema.** Import into `frame`, `frame_version`, and the existing related tables. Add job, lineage, row-error, and outbox storage. This keeps one authoritative history and limits migration work. It falls short if the application needs sites and specs to have independent identities and lifecycles in this release.
2. **Migrate to the proposed six-table model.** Make the six normalized tables the current inventory store and use `frame_history` for immutable historical data. This makes sites and specs first-class entities, but requires migrating existing reads and writes. History becomes unreliable if it points to mutable site or spec records without preserving their old values.
I’ll write the agreed architecture into the Technical Plan, using the existing versioned schema as the import target.

### Upload and dispatch

```text
Operator → web app → BFF → Spring Boot → import_jobs
Operator → presigned PUT → S3 → Lambda → SQS → Spring Boot → Temporal
                                  SQS retries → DLQ → dispatch reconciler
Temporal worker → pinned S3 object → PostgreSQL staging → inventory apply

Operator ← web app ← BFF ← Spring Boot job status and row errors

Expose job status, counts, fatal errors, and paginated row errors through the BFF.

The Lambda forwards object-created events. The Spring Boot consumer verifies the bucket, key, object version, and size, then conditionally records PENDING and starts Temporal workflow csv-import-{jobId}. Acknowledge the message after start succeeds or the consumer confirms that the same job already started. Retry with backoff. Before a DLQ event can fail a job, reconcile ambiguous workflow starts and check that the job is still dispatchable. Reconcile old AWAITING_UPLOAD and PENDING jobs against S3 and Temporal. Handle failures on the Lambda-to-SQS leg separately.

The Temporal worker reads the pinned object and streams logical CSV records into job- and attempt-scoped UNLOGGED staging. Heartbeats report progress and let the worker detect cancellation. Keep the EOF completion marker in the same unlogged storage as the data. Before apply, check the marker and staged counts. If a crash leaves staging incomplete or empty, reload from S3. Use the existing frame table for stable identity and frame_version for current and historical values. Resolve region, town, postcode, and format through existing lookup tables. Attach external references and ordered links to the resulting frame version. Add job, row error, scope watermark, outbox, and import lineage storage through Flyway. Close current versions and append replacements in separate set-based statements. Commit inventory, versioned references and links, outbox events, applicable scope watermark, and job result together. If the worker loses the commit response, return the stored result when it retries.

Keep staging outside the inventory lock. During promotion, take a shared transaction-scoped inventory lock for manual writes and DELTA and an exclusive lock for FULL_SNAPSHOT. Obtain frame locks in stable ID order. Evaluate scope membership, watermark checks, and retirement against the protected pre-apply view.

Require scope to be GLOBAL or a canonical country, country/region, or country/region/environment path. Use the explicit snapshot_as_of where available, otherwise derive it from MAX(modified_date) on the complete file. A broader snapshot can still apply its present rows under the ordinary conflict rules when a descendant has a newer watermark. Protect that entire descendant subtree from retirement.

3. **Define retirement ordering across all reactivation paths** (lines 67–73, Zoom Out). ## What this proposes

An authorized operator creates an import job in the application, uploads the CSV directly to S3, and checks progress, counts, and row errors in the application. An S3 notification reaches Spring Boot through SQS, which starts a Temporal workflow to stage and validate the accepted object version, then apply the changes and record the outcome in one transaction. The default `DELTA` mode applies eligible rows for named frames, with an authorized force option for conflicts and manual-deletion restoration. `FULL_SNAPSHOT` can also retire absent frames in one declared scope after checking the export watermark, frame presence, and retirement safeguards.

## How the existing system works, per this document

The application already supports editing individual frames. The `frame` table holds the stable frame identity, while `frame_version` holds current and historical values, with links and external references attached to each version and fields for the site and specification. Inventory writes use a lock on the stable frame identity and preserve the boundary between consecutive versions. Some existing manual versions inherited a source timestamp, and manual deletion can leave a frame with a historical version but no current version.

## Findings

- **Major — Export completeness, lines 47–51, 67–69, 112.** The staging completion marker verifies that the worker read the uploaded object to EOF. The snapshot rule additionally requires a complete export, but the document gives no way to recognize a syntactically valid file that stops early on a record boundary or omits part of its declared scope. A reader cannot tell what evidence satisfies this guard or what result to expect if the producer provides only a CSV.

- **Major — Canonical scope and malformed records, lines 51, 55, 65–69, 108, 112.** The document lists the allowed scope shapes but leaves the canonical values and normalization unspecified. It also says every record must be in scope and that identifiable malformed rows count as present. A reader cannot determine which location is authoritative when incoming scope fields are missing or malformed, or when an existing frame is moving between scopes. These cases determine whether the snapshot fails, protects a frame, or updates it.

- **Major — Legacy manual version identification, lines 49, 57, 99–100, 129.** The contrast between inherited `source_modified_at` and the effective `valid_from` baseline is clear. The document does not name an existing marker, provenance field, or classification rule that identifies versions with inherited timestamps. A reader cannot determine which records the migration changes or predict their import conflict behavior.

- **Major — Operator input for force and export time, lines 17–20, 41, 57–59, 67, 107–108, 119.** The service accepts a force flag and an explicit snapshot watermark, and both can materially affect the outcome. The frontend step mentions only collecting mode and scope. A reader cannot tell how an operator deliberately authorizes a forced correction or supplies a known export time in the application.

- **Major — Accepted CSV contract, lines 9, 17, 49–55, 111, 129.** The document names a supplied 45-field file and identifies some fields and mapping rules, but it does not link the supplied file or point to a field contract. A new reader has no direct reference for the required headers, frame identifier field, which fields may be empty, or supported date formats. That leaves the scope of row validation and the meaning of an actionable row error unclear.

- **Nit — Workflow terminology, lines 33–43, 55, 115–119.** The diagram shows where the BFF and DLQ sit in the upload path. Expanding BFF as the application's backend for frontend and DLQ as the dead-letter queue on first use would make their roles easier to follow before readers reach the implementation details.
EOF

# Goldfish Review: Loop (Orchestration Driver)

When running in Codex or ChatGPT Work, first read [Codex integration](../../docs/codex.md).
In Claude Code or Cowork, read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/claude.md` first.

## Overview

This skill acts as the central orchestration engine driving the multi-agent
review loop. It coordinates two distinct agent memory models:

*   **The Goldfish (Adversarial Auditors)**: Subagents spawned in isolated,
    fresh context windows to catch unstated assumptions without historical bias.
*   **The Elephant (Persistent Resolver)**: The primary agent context holding
    institutional knowledge to evaluate findings and apply approved repairs.

The driver manages argument intake, resolves paths for reviewers and standards,
unconditionally re-parses target line ranges before every iteration, spawns
concurrent specialized Goldfish auditors based on configuration, and coordinates
with the Elephant context to resolve findings.

## Delegation

A Goldfish runs in a fresh context with no conversation history. Spawn each
subagent with your harness's subagent tool (Antigravity: `invoke_subagent`; Claude Code: `Agent`; Codex: `spawn_agent`). Each subagent is defined in `agents/<file>.md`, and its
frontmatter `name` (for example `egm-zoom-out`) is the subagent type to request
where your harness registers named subagents. Otherwise spawn a general-purpose
subagent and tell it to read that persona file first. Pass the prompt verbatim
and wait for the report. If your harness cannot nest subagents,
use direct dispatch instead of the synthesizer. See `docs/harnesses.md`.
If your harness has no subagent tool, stop and tell the user: a review in the same
context is not a Goldfish review.

## Inputs

The caller or user provides exactly these parameters:

*   **`TargetFile`**: Absolute or relative path to target document.
*   **`SemanticTarget`**: Descriptive targeting string (e.g., *"Target the H4
    block with SS-ID 'S1.12'"*), or `full file`.
*   **`Reviewers`**: List of reviewer names (shortnames or paths).
*   **`Standards`**: Mapping of reviewer names to standard names (shortnames or
    paths).
*   **`GoldfishContext`**: A reading list (source files, directories, or
    documentation URLs) fed to reviewers to establish their baseline. An empty
    list from the caller counts as provided; do not ask for it again. Some
    reviewers cannot open URLs, so before the first round save the raw page of
    each URL as a new file in the working directory (or your harness's artifact
    directory) and pass its absolute path instead. If a page cannot be saved,
    ask the user for a local copy and end your turn; if no one can answer,
    as in a headless run, leave it out, tell the user, and keep going.

## Path & Standard Resolution Logic

When resolving names in `Reviewers` and `Standards`:

*   **Reviewer Shortnames**: Map reviewer shortname (e.g., `design_critic`,
    `structural`, `style`, `implementation_readiness`,
    `codebase_details`, `comprehension`, `zoom_out`) to `agents/{name}.md`.
    The persona file defines the reviewer's core mandates, audit vectors, and
    output format.
*   **Standard Shortnames**: Map standard shortname (e.g., `feature-spec-standard`,
    `implementation-readiness-standard`, `zoom-out-standard`, `heilmeier-standard`,
    `re-implementation-standard`) to `resources/document_standards/{name}.md`.
*   **Custom Paths**: If the name contains a slash (`/`), treat it as an
    absolute or workspace-relative path and read it directly.

## Execution Workflow

### Step 1: Intake & Configuration UX

Evaluate the provided inputs (`TargetFile`, `SemanticTarget`, `Reviewers`,
`Standards`, `GoldfishContext`).

1.  **Identify Missing Inputs**: Determine which of the required parameters are
    missing.
2.  **Interactive Onboarding**:
    *   If **all** inputs are present, proceed to Step 2.
    *   If **some or all** inputs are missing, interactively prompt the user
        **only for the missing inputs**, one at a time via chat messages.
3.  **Reviewer Recommendations**:
    *   *Feature Specs*: Recommend `design_critic` (mapped to
        `resources/document_standards/feature-spec-standard.md`) and
        `structural` (mapped to `resources/document_standards/feature-spec-standard.md`).
    *   *Implementation Plans*: Recommend `implementation_readiness`
        (mapped to `resources/document_standards/implementation-readiness-standard.md`)
        and `codebase_details`.
4.  **Confirm Configuration**: Display the consolidated plan (Target, Reviewers,
    and mapped Standards) and ask the user to confirm before proceeding.

### Step 2: The Sharpening Loop (Iterative Cycle)

Execute the following sequence in a continuous loop:

#### 2.1 Unconditional Target Resolution

Before every iteration, unconditionally re-scan `TargetFile` by reading it
and using the stable `SemanticTarget` string (e.g., locating the target header) to
dynamically determine the updated absolute start and end line numbers. This
ensures absolute accuracy even if the file was edited in prior rounds. (If `full
file` mode is specified, confirm full-file line bounds).

#### 2.2 Review Swarm Execution

1.  **Launch Subagent Swarm**:
    Spawn subagents to execute the review:
    *   **Hierarchical Dispatch (Synthesizer)**: Spawn the intermediate
        synthesizer subagent (`agents/synthesizer.md` / `egm-synthesizer`).
        The synthesizer spawns the Goldfish review swarm in
        parallel, deduplicates findings, writes the report artifact, and
        returns a single summary message to avoid context pollution in the root
        conversation. Pass it the Failed Reviewers rule below and
        `GoldfishContext`, and tell it to give those files to each reviewer.
        Its summary must give a status, `completed` or `not run`, for each
        requested reviewer.
    *   **Direct Dispatch (Flat Swarm)**: Alternatively, spawn each requested
        reviewer subagent in `Reviewers` directly.
        Instruct each subagent to first read its persona definition in
        `agents/{name}.md`, then audit `TargetFile` at the resolved line range
        against its designated standard in `resources/document_standards/`,
        supplying `GoldfishContext`.
    *   Each reviewer produces findings with severity (🔴 Blocker, 🟡 Major, 🟢
        Nit), line numbers, discrepancy descriptions, and rationales.
2.  **Consolidate Findings**: Collect all findings across reviewers into a single
    flat `FindingsList`. Give each finding a stable id
    (`<reviewer>-<round>-<n>`) and record its reviewer, severity, and affected
    scope.
3.  **Failed Reviewers**: A reviewer that times out, fails, or returns no report
    did not review. Retry it once. If it fails again, record it as **not run**
    in the report. Never count it as a reviewer with zero findings. If the
    synthesizer summary has no status for a requested reviewer, record that
    reviewer as not run.

#### 2.3 Aggregated Resolution Hand-off

1.  Pass `TargetFile`, the active line range, and the aggregated `FindingsList`
    to the **`egm-resolve`** workflow.
2.  Execute the resolution workflow in the primary Elephant context:
    *   Categorize findings into `CONTEST` vs. `PROPOSE FIX`.
    *   Save `goldfish_review_report.md` with your file-writing tool.
    *   Present the interactive decision gate (Auto accept, Continue, Interactive
        breakdown).
    *   Apply approved text repairs to `TargetFile` using your file-editing tool.

#### 2.4 Iteration Check & Turn Boundary

Fresh reviewers sample differently each round, so a round with zero findings
is rare even when the document improves. Use these rules instead:

*   **Settled findings**: A finding is settled when it is contested or
    recorded without a fix (accepted risk). Keep the settled list across
    rounds. If a new reviewer raises a settled finding again (same affected
    scope, same issue), do not re-open it.
*   **Fixed findings**: An applied fix does not settle a finding. If a later
    reviewer raises the same issue at the same scope, the fix failed or a
    later edit reintroduced the issue. Re-open the finding.
*   **Clean round**: A round is clean when no reviewer raises a Blocker or
    Major finding that is not settled. Nits do not block. A reviewer recorded
    as not run makes the round not clean. Decide this from the review results,
    before you apply the fixes of that round.
*   **Converged**: Two consecutive clean rounds. One clean round is not enough,
    because the next fresh reviewer can find a different gap in the same text.
*   **Cap**: 5 rounds.
*   **Churn**: A new finding is at the scope of an applied fix, and reverting
    that fix would resolve it.

On converged, go to Step 3. On cap or churn, write a short list of the open
findings by severity, then ask the user one question: accept and proceed,
continue past the cap, or return the document to drafting.

**Crucial Turn-Taking Requirement**: After the resolution phase finishes for a
given round, the loop driver **MUST respect the turn-taking checkpoint in
`egm-resolve`**. The driver must remain idle across human turns,
only looping back to Step 2.1 when the user explicitly confirms they wish to run
another round of review.

### Step 3: Output Boundary & Final Checkpoint

Upon completion (converged, cap or churn accepted by the user, or manual
halt):

*   **Programmatic Callers**: If running as a subflow of `egm-review`, exit
    cleanly to hand execution back to the parent workflow.
*   **Manual Invocations**: Output a summary of completion in chat: *"The review
    loop has completed after [N] rounds ([converged | accepted at cap | halted]).
Open findings are in the report. Would you like to proceed to
    the next stage, or do you have any final questions?"*

# Stage 8 — Intermediate Zoom Out

The reviewer read the [full design](docs/designs/bulk-csv-inventory-import-design.md), all 21 baseline files, and the Stage 5–7 reports. All context reads completed. The design is unchanged.

## Open blockers

1. **Snapshot completeness** (lines 47–51, 67–69). EOF and both percentage guards can accept a syntactically valid partial export. Bind trusted exporter scope, export time, record count, and digest to the pinned upload before enabling retirement. Plain CSV uploads can still use DELTA.
2. **Operator identity and authorization** (lines 17–20, 41, 108, 118). Specify verified identity at the BFF and Spring Boot boundary and permissions for creation, scope, force, and access to diagnostics. This also blocks the first DELTA release.

## New major findings

1. **Make lineage visible in history** (lines 9, 20, 55, 71, 99, 113, 118–119). A stored job ID alone cannot support operator traceability. Add a provenance projection to the current history RPC and GraphQL query, name the browser entry point, and define access to a job reference after row diagnostics expire.
2. **Define manual actions on retired frames** (lines 59, 65, 71–73, 113). The retired frame remains current and can be reached by direct lookup. Existing manual edit can reactivate it, and manual delete can convert it to a manual-deletion tombstone. Decide the intended transitions and verify them through the existing API.
3. **Use the supplied design system and frontend routing** (lines 113, 119). Specify reuse of the inventory shell, filters, status chips, and audit timeline. Extend the existing Next.js proxy to give the browser a same-origin route to the BFF.
4. **Clarify the upload size guarantee** (lines 41, 47, 123–124). Validation after object creation bounds processing, while a larger object may remain in S3 until cleanup. Bind a validated length to the signed request and verify browser support, or specify prompt cleanup of rejected objects and describe the limit as a processing cap.

## Remaining rollout risks

- **Snapshot ordering and scope** (lines 57, 65–73). Define the retirement watermark across all reactivation paths, scope keys and cross-scope moves, malformed scope fields, active statuses, and freshness and future-skew boundaries. Use a controlled clock for snapshot tests with the historical CSV.
- **Exclusive transaction work** (lines 47, 65–69, 95). Cap scoped work and timeout before enabling snapshots. Measure concurrent writer wait on representative inventory.
- **Dispatch and staging recovery** (lines 30–51, 83–85, 109–110). State what SQS and Temporal own, define the authoritative state at their handoff, and justify unlogged staging or compare logged staging.
- **Existing writer and RPC behavior** (lines 51, 55–61, 107–119). Share frame invariants and use existing RPC handling. Classify legacy manual versions with the available change-source markers, define fallback and equal-timestamp hashing, and include the new proto in BFF generation and packaging.
- **Local prerequisites and residual wording** (lines 18, 43, 119, 124–130). Verify a fresh-checkout run and object-version support. Keep the real AWS test. Remove the residual inventory-event goal, clarify acknowledgment at the SQS message boundary, and specify operator controls for force and export time.
EOF

input.title: Epic: Bulk CSV inventory import
input.description:
Let authorized inventory operators upload inventory_frame.csv, track progress, see actionable row errors, and trace accepted changes in frame history.

**Release 1 — DELTA.** Upload directly to versioned S3. Deliver notifications directly to SQS and start one Temporal workflow per job. Apply eligible rows to the existing PostgreSQL version history and commit the job result with the inventory changes. Replays must not create extra versions.

**Release 2 — FULL_SNAPSHOT.** Enable scoped retirement only after trusted export completeness, watermark ordering, and bounded retirement work are proven. Use country, region, and environment scopes as defined in the design.

**Done when:** An authorized operator imports the supplied 1,000-row CSV through the app, sees results and history, and can retry without duplicate versions. Snapshot rollout has its own safety and verification gate. First-release limits are 10 MiB, 10,000 data rows, and seven-day object and row diagnostic retention. Outbox work is deferred.

**Release 2 — FULL_SNAPSHOT**

- **GLO-33** — Implement scoped retirement and verify rollout safety

Snapshot implementation is blocked on both the safety contract and the DELTA release. Outbox work is deferred.
